## Frontend Architecture Summary: TaskAI

Based on my exploration of `/Users/anshumanbiswas/play/taskai/web`, here's a detailed breakdown of the TaskAI frontend architecture:

### 1. **Route Structure** (`src/routes/`)
**File: `/Users/anshumanbiswas/play/taskai/web/src/routes/`**

Main routes:
- **Landing.tsx** - Public landing page
- **Login.tsx, Signup.tsx, ForgotPassword.tsx, ResetPassword.tsx** - Auth flows
- **Dashboard.tsx** - Main app container with sidebar and layout
- **Projects.tsx** - List all user projects
- **ProjectDetail.tsx** (1013 lines) - **Main board view** - The most complex component
  - Tab-based design: board, wiki, settings
  - Kanban board with swim lanes
  - Filter bar (sprint, assignee, priority, label, task ID)
  - Drag-and-drop task management using dnd-kit
  - Mobile-responsive (tabs for lanes on mobile, grid on desktop)
- **Sprints.tsx, Tags.tsx** - Sprint/tag management
- **TaskDetail.tsx** - Detailed task modal/page
- **ProjectSettings.tsx** - Project settings and configurations
- **Admin.tsx** - Admin dashboard
- **Settings.tsx** - User settings
- **Wiki.tsx** - Wiki pages
- **Assets.tsx** - File/asset management
- **KnowledgeGraphPage.tsx** - Knowledge graph visualization
- **UserProfile.tsx** - User profile view

### 2. **UI Component Library** (`src/components/`)
**Pattern: Custom components + shadcn-inspired utilities**

Core UI components at `/Users/anshumanbiswas/play/taskai/web/src/components/ui/`:
- **Button.tsx** - Reusable button component
- **Card.tsx** - Card wrapper
- **TextInput.tsx** - Text input wrapper
- **FormError.tsx** - Error display
- **SearchSelect.tsx** - Dropdown with search
- **MultiSelectDropdown.tsx** - Multi-select dropdown (9.5KB)

Complex components:
- **Sidebar.tsx** - Project navigation sidebar
- **CommandPalette.tsx** - Cmd+K command palette
- **ProjectModal.tsx** - Create/edit project modal
- **MentionTextarea.tsx** - Rich text with mentions
- **WikiEditor.tsx** - Wiki content editor
- **WikiContent.tsx** - Wiki page renderer
- **ProtectedRoute.tsx** - Auth wrapper
- **SyncStatus.tsx** - Sync indicator
- **ProjectInvitationBanner.tsx** - Notification banner
- **ImagePickerModal.tsx** - Image selection
- **FigmaEmbed.tsx** - Figma embed support

**Inline Components in ProjectDetail.tsx:**
- **TaskColumn** - Swim lane column (droppable zone)
- **DraggableTask** - Task wrapper with drag listener
- **TaskCard** - Rendered task card with metadata
- **BoardFilterBar** - GitHub-style filter UI

### 3. **State Management** (`src/state/`)
**Pattern: React Context (no Redux/Zustand)**

- **AuthContext.tsx** - Authentication state
  - `useAuth()` hook provides: `user`, `loading`, `error`, `login()`, `signup()`, `logout()`, `clearError()`, `loginWithToken()`
  - Token stored in localStorage: `auth_token`
  
- **SyncContext.tsx** - Sync state (server-only, no RxDB)
  - `useSync()` hook provides: `syncState`, `triggerSync()`, `initializeSync()`, `destroySync()`
  
- **ThemeContext.tsx** - Dark/light theme toggle
  - CSS variable-driven (stored in `:root` selector)
  - Persisted to localStorage: `taskai_theme`
  - Theme class applied to `<html>` element

- **NotificationContext.tsx** - (exists, patterns in files)

**Data Persistence:**
- localStorage keys: `auth_token`, `taskai_theme`, `taskai_filters_${projectId}`, `sidebar-pinned-${userId}`
- No client-side caching layer; all data flows from API

### 4. **API Client** (`src/lib/api.ts`)
**File: `/Users/anshumanbiswas/play/taskai/web/src/lib/api.ts` (2050 lines)**

**Architecture:**
- Singleton `ApiClient` class with instance exported as `api`
- OpenAPI-generated types from backend spec (`src/lib/api.types.ts`)
- Token-based auth (Bearer token in Authorization header)
- Fetch-based (no axios)
- Error handling: JSON error responses parsed, HTTP errors throw

**Key features:**
- All API calls prefixed with `/api/`
- Automatic token injection from localStorage
- 404 handling + non-JSON response fallback
- Streaming support for GitHub sync with SSE (Server-Sent Events)

**Main endpoints organized by domain:**
- **Auth**: signup, login, getCurrentUser, updateProfile, changePassword, 2FA setup
- **Projects**: getProjects, getProject, createProject, updateProject, deleteProject
- **Tasks**: getTasks, createTask, updateTask, getTaskByNumber, deleteTask
- **Task Comments**: getTaskComments, createTaskComment, updateTaskComment, deleteTaskComment
- **Swim Lanes**: getSwimLanes, createSwimLane, updateSwimLane, deleteSwimLane
- **Sprints**: getSprints, createSprint, updateSprint, deleteSprint, shareSprint, unshareSprint
- **Tags**: getTags, createTag, updateTag, deleteTag, shareTag, unshareTag
- **Attachments**: getTaskAttachments, createTaskAttachment, deleteTaskAttachment
- **Wiki Pages**: getWikiPages, createWikiPage, getWikiPage, updateWikiPage, deleteWikiPage, getWikiPageContent, updateWikiPageContent, getWikiPageVersions, restoreWikiPageVersion, downloadWikiPagePdf, downloadWikiPageMarkdown, searchWiki, listWikiAnnotations, createWikiAnnotation, updateWikiAnnotation, deleteWikiAnnotation, createAnnotationComment, updateAnnotationComment, deleteAnnotationComment
- **GitHub**: getProjectGitHub, updateProjectGitHub, githubDiscoverMappings, githubSync (with streaming), githubOAuthInit, githubListRepos, githubDisconnect, githubGetMappings, githubSaveMappings, githubGetSyncLogs, githubPushTask, githubPushAll
- **Knowledge Graph**: getProjectGraph
- **Notifications**: getNotifications, getNotificationCount, markNotificationsRead, markAllNotificationsRead
- **User Profile**: getUserProfile, getUserActivityFeed
- **Team**: getMyTeam, getTeamMembers, inviteTeamMember, removeTeamMember, getMyInvitations, getMyTeamMemberships, acceptInvitation, rejectInvitation
- **Admin**: getUsers, getUserActivity, updateUserAdmin, deleteUser, adminUpdateUserProfile, adminResetPassword, adminGetInvitations, getAnalyticsOverview, getAnalyticsUsers, getAnalyticsUserDetail, getAnalyticsAPIKeys
- **Settings**: getCloudinaryCredential, saveCloudinaryCredential, deleteCloudinaryCredential, testCloudinaryConnection, getFigmaCredentials, saveFigmaCredentials, deleteFigmaCredentials, getFigmaEmbed, getBackupStatus, getBackupSettings, updateBackupSettings, triggerBackup, listBackupHistory, deleteBackupRecord, disconnectBackup, listBackupFolders, createBackupFolder, downloadBackupRecord, copyFromEnv
- **Assets**: getImages, getAssets, getStorageUsage, updateAttachment, deleteAttachment
- **Drawings**: getProjectDrawings, registerProjectDrawing
- **Invites**: getInvites, createInvite, validateInvite, adminBoostInvites
- **Email Provider**: getEmailProvider, saveEmailProvider, deleteEmailProvider, testEmailProvider
- **Reactions**: toggleReaction
- **Global Search**: globalSearch

**Custom hooks** (`src/lib/api.hooks.ts`):
- `useApi<T>(apiCall, deps)` - Generic fetch hook returning `{ data, loading, error, refetch }`
- `useProjects()` - Hook for fetching all projects
- `useProject(id)` - Hook for single project
- `useTasks(projectId)` - Hook for project tasks
- `useCreateProject()` - Hook for project creation

### 5. **Existing Board/Kanban Views**
**File: `/Users/anshumanbiswas/play/taskai/web/src/routes/ProjectDetail.tsx` (main implementation)**

**Architecture:**
- **Swim lanes** (columns) = status categories (todo, in_progress, done)
- Tasks drag-and-drop between lanes → updates `swim_lane_id` → backend auto-syncs status
- Responsive design:
  - **Desktop** (md breakpoint): CSS Grid with dynamic columns `grid-template-columns: repeat(${swimLanes.length}, minmax(0, 1fr))`
  - **Mobile** (< md): Select dropdown to view single lane at a time
  
**Features:**
- **Filtering**: Persisted to localStorage per project (`taskai_filters_${projectId}`)
  - Sprint filter
  - Assignee filter
  - Priority filter (urgent, high, medium, low)
  - Label/tag filter
  - Task ID filter (by task_number)
- **Task cards** display:
  - Task number (e.g., #42)
  - Task title
  - Assignee names (supports multiple assignees)
  - GitHub reactions (with emoji counts)
  - Opacity reduced for completed tasks
  - Hover effects (border color, shadow)

### 6. **Key UI Patterns**

**Drag-and-Drop:**
- Library: **@dnd-kit/core v6.3.1**, @dnd-kit/sortable v10.0.0
- PointerSensor with 8px activation distance
- DndContext wraps the board
- useDroppable on columns
- useDraggable on task cards
- DragOverlay renders dragging state
- Style transforms applied with `translate3d` for performance

**Modals:**
- **Task Detail Modal**: Overlay with semi-transparent backdrop
  - Rendered as portal via routes (App.tsx lines 106-114)
  - Background location state used for navigation
- **New Task Modal**: Fixed position modal in ProjectDetail
- **Project Modal**: Separate ProjectModal component

**Forms:**
- TextInput, SearchSelect components
- Controlled inputs with state
- Form validation before submission
- Loading states during async operations
- Error/success message display via FormError component

**Navigation:**
- React Router v6 with nested routes
- Tab-based navigation within ProjectDetail (board, wiki, settings)
- Search params for tab state (no browser state pollution)
- Modal overlay navigation pattern (backgroundLocation in state)

**Real-time Updates:**
- Server-Sent Events (SSE) for GitHub sync progress
- Optimistic updates in ProjectDetail (createTask, updateTask)
- Manual refetch triggers via API hook

**Responsive Design:**
- Tailwind CSS with md breakpoint (768px)
- Mobile-first with hidden/visible utilities
- Flexible grid layouts
- Touch-friendly interactions

### 7. **Styling System**
**File: `/Users/anshumanbiswas/play/taskai/web/tailwind.config.js`**

**Framework: Tailwind CSS v3.4.0**

**Color Scheme:**
- **Primary** (Linear-inspired purple): #5e6ad2 - used for active states, highlights, CTAs
- **Secondary** (Magenta): #d946ef
- **Success** (Green): #22c55e
- **Warning** (Yellow): #eab308
- **Danger** (Red): #ef4444
- **Dark semantic colors** (CSS variable-driven):
  - `dark-bg-{base,primary,secondary,tertiary,elevated}`
  - `dark-border-{subtle,medium,strong}`
  - `dark-text-{primary,secondary,tertiary,quaternary}`
  - Light mode overrides in `html.light` selector

**Typography:**
- Font family: Inter
- Custom font sizes: xs (0.75rem) → 6xl (3.75rem)
- Line heights and letter spacing configured

**Shadows:**
- `linear-sm` (1px 2px)
- `linear`, `linear-lg`, `linear-xl` (depth progression)

**Animations:**
- fade-in, slide-up, slide-down (0.15s-0.2s)

**Custom Scrollbar:**
- Width: 8px
- Dark-themed styling
- Hover states

**File: `/Users/anshumanbiswas/play/taskai/web/src/index.css`**
- Base layer with CSS variable definitions
- Light/dark theme switching via `html.light` class
- Custom scrollbar styling
- Prose (markdown) styling

### 8. **Key Patterns for Building Roadmap Feature**

**Recommended patterns to follow:**

1. **Routing**: Add route `/app/projects/:projectId/roadmap` in App.tsx, create `Roadmap.tsx` component in routes/
2. **Tab integration**: Add roadmap tab button in ProjectDetail.tsx header alongside board/wiki
3. **State management**: Use React Context if global, or component state with localStorage for persistence
4. **API calls**: Extend `api.ts` with roadmap endpoints following existing pattern (getProjectRoadmap, updateRoadmap, etc.)
5. **Drag-and-drop**: Leverage dnd-kit as used in board (same library, patterns)
6. **Filtering**: Mirror BoardFilterBar pattern for timeline/roadmap filters
7. **Components**: Create reusable components for:
   - RoadmapTimeline (or Gantt chart component)
   - RoadmapPhase/Milestone card
   - RoadmapHeader with filter bar
8. **Styling**: Use dark-bg-*, dark-text-*, dark-border-* utilities from Tailwind config
9. **Loading/Error states**: Follow ProjectDetail pattern (skeleton loader, error boundary)
10. **Responsive design**: Mobile dropdown/modal for roadmap view (like swim lane selector)

**Architecture file locations:**
- New route: `/Users/anshumanbiswas/play/taskai/web/src/routes/Roadmap.tsx`
- API extensions: `/Users/anshumanbiswas/play/taskai/web/src/lib/api.ts` (add roadmap methods)
- Types: `/Users/anshumanbiswas/play/taskai/web/src/lib/api.ts` (add Roadmap, RoadmapPhase interfaces)
- Hooks: `/Users/anshumanbiswas/play/taskai/web/src/lib/api.hooks.ts` (add useRoadmap, useCreateRoadmapPhase, etc.)
- Components: `/Users/anshumanbiswas/play/taskai/web/src/components/` (create RoadmapCard, RoadmapTimeline, etc.)

**Handler Function Signature**:
```go
func (s *Server) HandleCreateTask(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
    ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(r.Context(), 5*time.Second)
    defer cancel()
    
    userID := r.Context().Value(UserIDKey).(int64)
    projectID, _ := strconv.ParseInt(chi.URLParam(r, "projectId"), 10, 64)
    
    // 1. Verify access
    hasAccess, _ := s.checkProjectAccess(ctx, userID, projectID)
    if !hasAccess {
        respondError(w, http.StatusForbidden, "access denied", "forbidden")
        return
    }
    
    // 2. Parse request
    var req CreateTaskRequest
    _ = json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&req)
    
    // 3. Validate
    if req.Title == "" {
        respondError(w, http.StatusBadRequest, "required", "invalid_input")
        return
    }
    
    // 4. Create via Ent ORM
    task, _ := s.db.Client.Task.Create().
        SetProjectID(projectID).
        SetTitle(req.Title).
        Save(ctx)
    
    // 5. Respond
    respondJSON(w, http.StatusCreated, task)
}
```

## AI-First Roadmap Feature: Implementation Plan

### Architecture Overview

The roadmap feature introduces three new domain concepts -- **Milestones** (epic-level groupings), **Task Dependencies** (blocks/blocked-by), and **AI Insights** (computed suggestions) -- layered on top of the existing Task/Sprint/SwimLane/Project model. The frontend adds a new top-level route per project (`/app/projects/:projectId?tab=roadmap`) with three sub-views: Timeline, Board, and List.

---

### Phase 1: Foundation (Data Model + CRUD + Basic Timeline)

#### 1A. New Database Tables

**Migration 065_milestones_and_dependencies.sql** (both SQLite and PostgreSQL variants in `api/internal/db/migrations/` and `api/internal/db/migrations/postgres/`)

**Table: `milestones`**
```sql
CREATE TABLE milestones (
    id          BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    project_id  BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    name        TEXT NOT NULL,
    description TEXT,
    color       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '#5e6ad2',
    target_date TIMESTAMPTZ,
    status      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'active',  -- active | completed | cancelled
    sort_order  INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    updated_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()
);
CREATE INDEX idx_milestones_project ON milestones(project_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_milestones_status ON milestones(status);
```

**Table: `task_dependencies`**
```sql
CREATE TABLE task_dependencies (
    id              BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    task_id         BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES tasks(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    depends_on_id   BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES tasks(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    dependency_type TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'blocks', -- blocks | related
    created_at      TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
    UNIQUE(task_id, depends_on_id)
);
CREATE INDEX idx_task_deps_task ON task_dependencies(task_id);
CREATE INDEX idx_task_deps_depends ON task_dependencies(depends_on_id);
```

**Alter `tasks` table** -- add `milestone_id`:
```sql
ALTER TABLE tasks ADD COLUMN milestone_id BIGINT REFERENCES milestones(id) ON DELETE SET NULL;
CREATE INDEX idx_tasks_milestone ON tasks(milestone_id);
```

**Design rationale:** Milestones belong to a project, not a sprint. Tasks can belong to both a milestone (the "what") and a sprint (the "when"). Dependencies are directional: `task_id` is blocked by `depends_on_id`. The `dependency_type` column allows future expansion (e.g., "related" links).

#### 1B. Ent Schemas

**New file: `api/ent/schema/milestone.go`**
- Fields: id, project_id, name, description, color, target_date, status, sort_order, created_at, updated_at
- Edges: `From("project", Project.Type).Ref("milestones")`, `To("tasks", Task.Type)`
- Indexes: project_id, status

**New file: `api/ent/schema/taskdependency.go`**
- Fields: id, task_id, depends_on_id, dependency_type, created_at
- Edges: `From("task", Task.Type).Ref("dependencies")`, `From("depends_on", Task.Type).Ref("dependents")`
- Indexes: (task_id, depends_on_id) unique

**Modify: `api/ent/schema/task.go`**
- Add field: `field.Int64("milestone_id").Optional().Nillable()`
- Add edges: `edge.From("milestone", Milestone.Type).Ref("tasks").Unique().Field("milestone_id")`, `edge.To("dependencies", TaskDependency.Type)`, `edge.To("dependents", TaskDependency.Type)`

**Modify: `api/ent/schema/project.go`**
- Add edge: `edge.To("milestones", Milestone.Type)`

After schema changes, run `go generate ./ent` to regenerate the Ent client.

#### 1C. API Handlers

**New file: `api/internal/api/milestone_handlers.go`**

Follows the exact pattern of `sprint_tag_handlers.go` -- request/response structs at top, then handler methods on `*Server`.

Endpoints (registered in `api/cmd/api/main.go` inside the protected group):

### Key Design Decisions

**Why milestones are project-scoped, not sprint-scoped:** Milestones represent outcomes ("Launch v2.0") that span multiple sprints. Tasks belong to both a milestone and a sprint. This preserves the existing sprint workflow while adding a higher-level planning layer.

**Why dependencies use a junction table instead of a JSON array:** Proper foreign keys enable cascade deletes, cycle detection via recursive CTEs, and efficient querying of "what blocks this task" and "what does this task block" in both directions.

**Why capacity planning is algorithmic first, not LLM-first:** Sprint capacity math is deterministic. An LLM adds latency and unpredictability for no benefit. The LLM is reserved for tasks that genuinely require reasoning: generating roadmaps from goals, refining estimates from task descriptions, and explaining "why" a milestone is at risk.

**Why the timeline uses CSS grid instead of a library (vis-timeline, gantt-chart-d3, etc.):** The existing codebase has zero charting dependencies. A CSS grid timeline with SVG dependency arrows gives full design control, matches the dark Linear-inspired theme exactly, and avoids a 100KB+ dependency for what is fundamentally a horizontal bar layout.

**Why no separate "Epic" entity:** Milestones serve the same purpose. Adding both epics and milestones creates confusion about hierarchy. If sub-grouping within milestones is needed later, add a `parent_milestone_id` self-reference.

```sql

    id          BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    project_id  BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES projects(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    name        TEXT NOT NULL,
    description TEXT,
    color       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '#5e6ad2',

CREATE INDEX idx_milestones_status ON milestones(status);
```

```sql

    id              BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
    task_id         BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES tasks(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    depends_on_id   BIGINT NOT NULL REFERENCES tasks(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,

    { "type": "no_estimate", "count": 3, "message": "3 tasks have no estimated hours" }
  ]
}
```

Capacity computation logic:
- Each team member's capacity = sprint duration in working days * 8 hours (configurable per-member later)
- Allocated = sum of `estimated_hours` for tasks assigned to that member in that sprint
- Over/under = difference

```
GET /projects/{projectId}/roadmap/velocity
```

Response: average tasks completed per sprint, average story points per sprint, trend (improving/declining/stable), projected completion dates for each active milestone.

#### 2B. AI Suggestion Engine

**New file: `api/internal/ai/roadmap_suggestions.go`**

This is the AI-native piece. It uses the existing `embeddingClient` (Ollama) for local inference, or can be extended to call Claude API for richer suggestions.

```
POST /projects/{projectId}/roadmap/suggestions
```

Request body:
```json
{
  "type": "rebalance_sprint" | "estimate_tasks" | "predict_milestone" | "generate_roadmap",
  "context": { "sprint_id": 1, "milestone_id": 2 }
}
```

**Suggestion types (incremental build):**

1. **`rebalance_sprint`** (algorithmic, no LLM needed): Given a sprint with over-allocated members, suggest moving tasks to under-allocated members or the next sprint. Uses greedy bin-packing by estimated hours.

2. **`estimate_tasks`** (LLM-enhanced): For tasks without estimated_hours, use historical data (average hours for similar tasks by tag/priority/assignee) as a baseline. Optionally call Ollama/Claude to refine based on task title and description similarity.

3. **`predict_milestone`** (algorithmic + trend): Based on velocity (completed tasks per sprint in the last N sprints), predict when a milestone's remaining tasks will be done. Output: predicted completion date, confidence interval, "on track" / "at risk" / "behind" status.

4. **`generate_roadmap`** (LLM-required, Phase 3): Given a natural language project description, generate milestones and task stubs. This calls Claude API via the existing pattern (or Ollama for self-hosted).

#### 2C. Frontend -- AI Panel

**New file: `web/src/components/RoadmapAIPanel.tsx`**

A slide-out panel (or collapsible sidebar within the roadmap view) that shows:
- Capacity bar charts per sprint (simple SVG bars, no charting library)
- Velocity sparkline (last 6 sprints)
- AI suggestions as actionable cards: "Sprint 5 is 115% allocated. Rebalance?" with an "Apply" button that calls the rebalance endpoint and then updates tasks via PATCH
- Milestone health indicators (green/yellow/red) based on prediction

**New file: `web/src/components/CapacityChart.tsx`**
- Per-member horizontal stacked bars showing allocated vs capacity
- Color coding: green (<80%), yellow (80-100%), red (>100%)

**Modify: `web/src/routes/Roadmap.tsx`**
- Add AI panel toggle button in the toolbar
- Integrate capacity and suggestion data

---

### Phase 3: Advanced Features

#### 3A. Natural Language Roadmap Generation

Extend `POST /projects/{projectId}/roadmap/suggestions` with `type: "generate_roadmap"`:
- Input: free-text goal description ("Build a mobile app with auth, payments, and social features by Q3")
- Output: suggested milestones with task stubs, dates, and dependencies
- User reviews and applies with one click (batch create milestones + tasks)

#### 3B. Dependency Critical Path

**New endpoint: `GET /projects/{projectId}/roadmap/critical-path`**

Computes the longest chain of dependent tasks (critical path) and returns it highlighted. The timeline view renders these tasks in a distinct color. Any delay on the critical path delays the project.

Algorithm: topological sort of task dependency DAG, then longest path from source to sink.

#### 3C. What-If Scenarios

Allow users to create a "draft" roadmap (stored client-side or as a snapshot) where they can move tasks, change assignments, adjust dates, and see the capacity/prediction impact before committing changes.

#### 3D. MCP AI Tools

Add to `mcp/src/index.ts`:
- `suggest_sprint_rebalance` -- calls the rebalance suggestion endpoint
- `predict_milestone_completion` -- calls the prediction endpoint  
- `generate_roadmap_from_goal` -- calls the LLM generation endpoint
- `get_capacity_report` -- returns capacity analysis for a sprint

---

### File Inventory and Sequencing

**Phase 1 files (strict order):**

1. `api/internal/db/migrations/065_milestones_and_dependencies.sql` + postgres variant
2. `api/ent/schema/milestone.go` (new)

17. `web/src/routes/Roadmap.tsx` (new)
18. `web/src/routes/TaskDetail.tsx` (modify -- milestone + dependency sections)
19. `web/src/App.tsx` (modify -- add route)
20. `web/src/components/Sidebar.tsx` (modify -- add nav item)
21. `mcp/src/index.ts` (modify -- add milestone + dependency tools)

**Phase 2 files:**
22. `api/internal/api/roadmap_ai_handlers.go` (new)

**Phase 3 files:**

### Key Design Decisions

**Why milestones are project-scoped, not sprint-scoped:** Milestones represent outcomes ("Launch v2.0") that span multiple sprints. Tasks belong to both a milestone and a sprint. This preserves the existing sprint workflow while adding a higher-level planning layer.

**Why dependencies use a junction table instead of a JSON array:** Proper foreign keys enable cascade deletes, cycle detection via recursive CTEs, and efficient querying of "what blocks this task" and "what does this task block" in both directions.

**Why capacity planning is algorithmic first, not LLM-first:** Sprint capacity math is deterministic. An LLM adds latency and unpredictability for no benefit. The LLM is reserved for tasks that genuinely require reasoning: generating roadmaps from goals, refining estimates from task descriptions, and explaining "why" a milestone is at risk.

**Why the timeline uses CSS grid instead of a library (vis-timeline, gantt-chart-d3, etc.):** The existing codebase has zero charting dependencies. A CSS grid timeline with SVG dependency arrows gives full design control, matches the dark Linear-inspired theme exactly, and avoids a 100KB+ dependency for what is fundamentally a horizontal bar layout.

**Why no separate "Epic" entity:** Milestones serve the same purpose. Adding both epics and milestones creates confusion about hierarchy. If sub-grouping within milestones is needed later, add a `parent_milestone_id` self-reference.

input.content:
# Roadmap Feature Plan

## Context

TaskAI currently has **Board** (kanban) and **Wiki** tabs per project. The user wants a third top-level feature: **Roadmap** — a modern, AI-first planning view that sits above individual tasks and sprints, providing milestone-level planning, dependency tracking, capacity analysis, and AI-powered suggestions.

The roadmap bridges the gap between tactical task management (existing board) and strategic planning. It answers: "When will we ship X?", "Is the team overloaded?", and "What's blocking progress?"

---

## Phase 1: Foundation (Data Model + CRUD + Timeline UI)

### 1.1 Database Migration (`api/internal/db/migrations/064_milestones_and_dependencies.sql`)

**New table: `milestones`** — project-scoped epic-level groupings
```sql
milestones(id, project_id FK, name, description, color, target_date, status[active|completed|cancelled], sort_order, created_at, updated_at)
```

**New table: `task_dependencies`** — directional blocks/blocked-by
```sql
task_dependencies(id, task_id FK, depends_on_id FK, dependency_type[blocks|related], created_at, UNIQUE(task_id, depends_on_id))
```

**Alter `tasks`** — add `milestone_id BIGINT REFERENCES milestones(id) ON DELETE SET NULL`

**Design:** Milestones are project-scoped (not sprint-scoped). A task can belong to both a milestone ("the what") and a sprint ("the when"). Dependencies are stored relationally for cascade deletes and cycle detection via recursive CTEs.

### 1.2 Ent Schemas

| File | Action |
|------|--------|

All three packages build cleanly. Here's a summary of everything implemented:

## Phase 1 Complete: Roadmap Feature

### Backend (Go)
- **Migration 064/065**: `milestones` table, `task_dependencies` table, `tasks.milestone_id` column

# Codex Review

Target: working tree diff

The roadmap changes introduce a cross-project milestone assignment hole, inaccurate milestone progress stats for single-assignee tasks, and an edit flow that cannot clear existing milestone fields. Those are functional regressions, so the patch should not be considered correct.

Full review comments:

  `HandleCreateTask`/`HandleUpdateTask` now write any `milestone_id` straight onto the task without checking that the milestone belongs to the same project. Because the FK only references `milestones(id)`, a caller who knows another project's milestone ID can attach it here; `HandleListTasks` will then expose that foreign milestone name on project A, and `HandleListMilestones`/`HandleGetMilestoneProgress` for project B will count task data from the wrong project.

- [P2] Include legacy single-assignee tasks in milestone assignee stats — /Users/anshumanbiswas/play/taskai/api/internal/api/milestone_handlers.go:524-529
  `HandleGetMilestoneProgress` builds `by_assignee` exclusively from `task_assignees`, but the rest of the task API still treats `tasks.assignee_id` as the assignee source when no join-table rows exist (see the backfill in `HandleListTasks`). Any milestone containing older tasks or tasks created with only `assignee_id` will therefore under-report assignee stats even though those tasks show as assigned elsewhere.

- [P2] Preserve clearing of milestone fields from the edit modal — /Users/anshumanbiswas/play/taskai/web/src/components/roadmap/MilestoneModal.tsx:68-73
  Blanking an existing description or target date in the roadmap modal will not actually remove it: the modal serializes an empty description as `undefined` and a cleared date as `null`, while `HandleUpdateMilestone` only updates/clears those fields when it receives a non-nil string. After saving an edit with those inputs emptied, reopening the milestone still shows the old values.

content.text:
All three Codex review issues fixed:

1. **P1 — Cross-project milestone assignment**: Added validation in both `HandleCreateTask` and `HandleUpdateTask` that checks the milestone's `project_id` matches the task's project before allowing assignment. Returns `400 Bad Request` if they don't match.

2. **P2 — Legacy assignee missing from stats**: Rewrote the `HandleGetMilestoneProgress` assignee query to use a CTE that UNIONs `task_assignees` with legacy `tasks.assignee_id` (only for tasks that have no `task_assignees` rows), so older single-assignee tasks are counted.

3. **P2 — Can't clear description/target_date**: 
   - Backend: `HandleUpdateMilestone` now calls `ClearDescription()` when an empty string is received (instead of setting it to empty)
   - Frontend: `MilestoneModal` now sends empty string (not `undefined`) for cleared description and target_date when editing, so the backend knows to clear them.

- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, use Config tool.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (triggers) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/triggers.
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching.
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- guide: Create and edit guides on anshumanbiswas.com. Guides are educational, information-dense long-form content (not personal blog posts). Handles go-draw diagrams, footnote references, guide CRUD via API, and content formatting. Use when the user says "guide", "create a guide", "edit guide", or "/guide".
- dev-server: Start a local development server for any project with a .me.sh adapter. Handles Docker postgres, frontend dev server pointing to any environment (prod/staging/uat/local), and backend services. Use when the user says "start server", "run locally", "dev server", "local dev", "start local", "point to prod", "point to staging", or "/dev-server".
- rust-preflight: Run local pre-flight checks on a Rust workspace (or blue-stack) before pushing so that fast, deterministic failures (cargo fmt, cargo check / clippy, stale sqlx-data.json, missing migrations) are caught locally instead of burning a 5–10 minute CI cycle. MANDATORY before every `git push` that touches Rust/SQL/Cargo.toml/sqlx-data.json in the blue-stack workspace — do not skip it even when the user says "push" or "PR now". Also run after touching Rust/SQL files, or whenever the user says "preflight", "pre-push check", "will CI pass", "check before pushing", or "/rust-preflight".
- scrape-educative: Scrape educative.io courses and import into local learn.biswas.me. Auto-extracts cookies from Chrome, supports batch scraping with sorting. Use when the user says "scrape", "import course", "scrape educative", "get more courses", or "/scrape-educative".
- weekly-summary: Generate weekly CEO summary of team accomplishments across blue-stack repos. Supports date ranges: week (default), month, or custom date range. Use when the user says "weekly summary", "monthly summary", "team update", "CEO update", "what did the team do", "summary for <period>", "/weekly-summary", or provides team updates to summarize.
- deploy-learn: Deploy learn.biswas.me to production and sync local courses. Handles building Docker image on prod server, deploying container, exporting local courses, and importing to production. Use when user says "deploy learn", "push to production", "sync courses", "export courses", or "/deploy-learn".

- blog: Create and edit blog posts on anshumanbiswas.com. Handles go-draw diagrams (create, populate, embed), footnote references, post CRUD via API, cover image upload, and content formatting.
